_comment: Adapter-specific declarations for the fleet tooling (Entwicklung/scripts). They live HERE so that a change in this adapter never touches the locked tooling. Readers: sync-iopackage-from-i18n.py (manifestI18n, release gate B03) and submit-stable.py (forumThread). Keys starting with an underscore are comments.

manifestI18n._comment: instanceObjects id -> key in admin/i18n/<lang>.json. Every manifest object needs a `name` entry (an object without one is a structural error, and so is an entry whose object no longer exists); `desc` only where the name does not already say it - an empty desc beats an invented sentence.

name._note: The info channel was the one unmapped manifest object of the fleet run on 2026-09-05; admin/i18n already carried the key.

_listenPorts: The HA emulation listens on the TCP port of native.port — default 8123 like Home Assistant, changeable since K3 (krobi 2026-11-11 19:31); the admin's port-conflict check reads native.port + native.bind.
_deviceIds: Package check device-id-scheme: a display names no serial number on its first request, and often no model. hassemu assigns the id on that request (acceptance page K7, krobi 2026-11-11 19:51): the model the Android app names in its User-Agent, else `display`, then a hyphen and four characters hassemu draws itself, a counter when the id is taken; bound to the display's cookie, it never changes. Up to 1.46.1 the id was six random hex characters; such a display moves once to `display-<its last four>`.

deviceIds.assigned: src/lib/display-id.ts newDisplayId (model from the Android app's User-Agent, else `display`, plus randomIdTail: crypto.randomBytes(2), four hex characters, a counter when taken), called by src/lib/client-registry.ts freshClientId and bound to the display's cookie

_suites: Fleet suites of test/fleet-suites.js. connectionTest and groupSwitches: the settings page has no sendTo field, no device manager and no switch that adds or removes a group of datapoints. rename: under INVENTORY_RENAME=1 the fixture's reverse DNS gives one display a new hostname, and the display's automatic name follows it (client-registry applyHostname). dropDevice: no datapoint says whether a display is reachable — hassemu cannot know whether a display is connected right now (krobi 2026-08-27), so no display can be shown as gone. rejectLogin: hassemu logs in nowhere — the password in native protects the emulation itself, the displays log in to it.

connectionTest.none: the settings page has no sendTo field and the adapter has no device manager — there is no connection test to press

groupSwitches.none: no setting adds or removes a group of datapoints — the tree is one device per display

rejectLogin.none: hassemu logs in to no counterpart — its password protects the emulation itself, and the displays log in to hassemu

dropDevice.none: no datapoint says whether a display is reachable — hassemu cannot know whether a display is connected right now (krobi 2026-08-27)

serverTest._why: Proves the emulation answers on the server: the web server is up, every known display still reports its address, and a display setting written by hand is taken and confirmed. The server id lives in the instance data folder since B3 (krobi 2026-11-11 19:31) and is no datapoint to read.

_noDeviceSources: Gate A15: hassemu has no device catalog to keep current — every Home Assistant client (companion app on a wall display, tablet or phone) is served the same way and keyed by its cookie, never by a model. Needs krobi's grant ($fleetNone), requested through the Werkbank.
noDeviceSources: hassemu keeps no device catalog — every Home Assistant client is served the same way and identified by its cookie, never by a model
